Clips this one nicely through mid-wicket for a couple.
Drifting in towards Chandimal who eases it to short mid-wicket.
Loopy once again, Chandimal lunges forward in defense.
Tossed up delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
Nippy delivery at 140 clicks in the zone of apprehension. Mathews keeps his bat inside the line this time and lets it go. A testing comeback over from Ishant, a maiden.
Short of a length delivery, blocked watchfully.
Another nervy moment! Sharma has been troubling Mathews a lot. In the corridor of uncertainty, Angelo fishes at it and is too late to withdraw his bat. Gets beaten convincingly.

Oh, so close! Back of a length delivery outside off, keeps low. Mathews shapes for the cut but ends up getting a bottom edge that rolls past the stumps and towards the keeper. He could have easily chopped that back on.
On a length this time, Mathews covers the line and blocks it.
Short of a length delivery, blocked off the back foot.
Ishant Sharma is back on.
On the pads, worked past short leg for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Similar delivery, tapped to the same region.
This fullish delivery is eased to mid off.
Quick and flat, kept out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fullish in length, eased to mid off.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Fullish delivery, Chandimal clips it through square leg. Dhawan covers a lot of distance to his right and stops it. Two runs taken.
Fullish delivery outside off, left alone.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

Almost another wicket! Shami bangs in a bouncer outside off, Mathews goes for the pull but fails to get on top of the bounce. His bottom hand also comes off and the ball lobs in the air towards wide mid on. Vijay backtracks from short mid-wicket but can only see it fall down on the ground.
Very full on middle, jammed to covers.
Quicker on off, blocked nicely.
A bit slower in pace, kept out.
Silly point has moved to short leg.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and onto the ground.
Similar delivery, Chandimal looks to whip it but gets it off the inner half towards short fine leg.
Fired in on off, tucked to mid-wicket.
Full length ball on off, eased off the front foot to mid off.
This fullish delivery is eased to mid on.
Fuller in length this time, Mathews pushes at it but gets an inside edge through square leg. Two runs taken.
Good length delivery on off, defended solidly off the back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short of a length delivery, kept out nicely.
Eased to covers this time.
In line of the stumps, blocked watchfully.
Time for drinks. Meanwhile, the skipper, Dinesh Chandimal strides out to bat. He played well in the last Test but he needs to do much more than that in this game. Sri Lanka are in deep trouble.

OUT! Judicious use of the review from India! Jadeja strikes. He was causing problems for Dilruwan and he finally gets the better of him. Jadeja spots Perera use his feet once more and bowls the arm delivery. It skids on, beats the defense of Perera and pings him on the front pad. Up go the Indians in unison and Nigel Llong after thinking a bit shakes his head. Kohli has a chat with Jadeja and Saha and challenges the decision. Has coming down the track saved Perera again? Time for the replays. Hawk Eye shows three reds and the batsman is a goner. Earlier as well, Llong had adjudged him not out as he was down the track and the three-meter rule saved the batsman then. Not this time though as the commentators on air mention that Perera was 2.99 meters down the track. So, it was a matter of 1 centimeter which proved to be Perera's undoing. These little things in cricket can make a lot of difference. The Indians rejoice. The visitors are still behind by 461 runs!
Review time! The Indians think, discuss and ponder and eventually decide to review the LBW decision against Dilruwan Perera.
The slider this time, around the pads. Perera looks to clip it away but is hit on the pads.
Similar delivery, jammed out nicely.
Fullish delivery, eased back to Jadeja.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Streaky runs! On a good length outside off, Mathews pushes at it but gets it off the outer half past the gap between third slip and gully for another boundary.
On a length outside off, kept out off the front foot.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
FOUR! Straight as an arrow! Fullish delivery in line of the stumps, Mathews stays well-balanced and drives it past the outstretched right hand of Shami and races to the fence.
Back of a length on middle, nudged to mid-wicket.
Change of ends for Mohammed Shami.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.

FOUR! Hit with authority! Slow through the air, Perera dances down the track and lifts it over the bowler for a boundary. The 50-run stand comes up with that. However, they still have a lot of work to do.
Perera whacks this one and hits Murali Vijay straight on the pads at silly point.
Fullish delivery, eased off the front foot down the track.
Arm delivery, Perera advances down the track but gets hit on the pads.
Quick through the air, kept out nicely.
Back of a length delivery, defended solidly off the back foot.
Stays back to the length delivery and keeps it out watchfully.
Fullish delivery, patted to mid-wicket.
Shortish delivery around the pads, tucked away around the corner for a run.

Russel Arnold and Mathew Hayden make a good analysis. The reason why Perera is struggling is due to his lack of footwork. He plays away from the body with minimal feet movement and his head position is not correct. As a result, false strokes are induced. He has already been dropped once in the slip region.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Nicely controlled! Shortish delivery around off, Perera glides it nicely behind point and gets the desired result.
That turned and gripped! That will create doubts in mind of Mathews who is already fidgety. Quicker through the air on off, Mathews prods forward to defend but gets beaten by the away turn.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Works it with the angle towards wide mid on for a single.
FOUR! Runs continue to flow from Perera's bat. Tossed up delivery, Perera creams it through covers. Dhawan from the same region hares after it but once again fails to stop the boundary.

Another appeal for an LBW is denied! Jadeja watches Perera use his feet and hence shortens the length. It hits him on the pad first and then the bat. Indians are confident but the umpire shakes his head. Replays show that the impact was umpire's call as the point of contact on the pads was more than three meters and would have gone over the stumps.
Floated delivery, Perera lunges forward in defense.
On a length outside off, pushed off the outer half to gully.
Short of a length delivery, Angelo gets on top of the bounce and blocks it stoutly.
Back of a length ball on middle, defended solidly off the back foot.
Fullish delivery, nudged to mid-wicket.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Mathews' trouble around the off stump continues. In the zone outside off, Mathews plays it away from the body compulsively and and gets beaten.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Fires this at 87 kph but down the leg side, Perera just uses of the pace of the delivery and tickles it past the keeper for a boundary.
Plays this one with soft hands to covers.
Tossed up outside off, hit hard to extra cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

A loud appeal for an LBW is turned down! Quicker in pace around off, Perera skips down the track but fails to defend it. Wears it on the pads and Jadeja puts up a confident appeal. The umpire stays unmoved though. Replays show it would have missed the stumps.
Fullish on middle, eased to mid on.
Time for spin. Ravindra Jadeja comes into the attack. More importantly, the man with the safe pair of hands, Ajinkya Rahane is stationed at first slip.

FOUR! Third boundary in the over, all scored by Mathews. This will be a confidence booster. Fullish on middle, Mathews comes forward and strokes it past a diving Ashwin at mid on to find the fence. 12 from the over.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! This is sublime! Timing and grace written all over that one. Fuller in length on off, Mathews creams it through mid off. Dhawan hares after it but only comes second best.
FOUR! That will come as a relief to Mathews! Sharma slips this one down the leg side, Mathews tucks it nicely through square leg for a boundary.
Full length delivery on middle, eased off the front to mid on.
The edges keep coming! In the zone of apprehension, Mathews gets opened up and flirts with it. Gets an outside edge which falls short of Rahane at gully. He seems in absolute disarray at the moment.
On a length on off, Dilruwan defends it solidly from the crease.
Bouncer this time, Perera ducks under it.
On a length, Perera covers the line and defends it stoutly.
FOUR! Nicely done! Fuller in length outside off, Perera drives it on the up through cover-point and the ball races to the fence.
Fullish in length, defended solidly off the front foot.
Back of a length outside off, played off the outer half to point.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On a length around off, Angelo fiddles with it and gets it off the outer half towards first slip.
Fullish on middle and leg, eased to mid-wicket.

DROPPED! That is as easy a chance you will get at this level. Good length delivery around off, holding its line. Mathews pokes at it yet again and this time the ball catches the outside edge of the bat. It is flying towards Kohli at second slip who is a bit late to react. Moves to his left and bends low but fails to hold onto it. Actually, the ball hit his wrist and rolled away. He is down on the ground and is really disappointed. He is looking at his hands in anger. No excuse for that one. Mathews is leading a charmed life.
Third slip in place now. Rohit Sharma is the man there. India on attacking mode.
Another brute of a delivery! Good length delivery in the corridor of uncertainty, moves away after pitching. Mathews has no option but to play at it. Gets foxed though.
Mathews gets beaten again! Poor cricket from him. This one is wide outside off and Mathews fishes at it again and misses.
On a length, shaping in. Angelo tucks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Indecision from Mathews! Shortish delivery outside off, Mathews tries to duck under it initially but fails to take his bat out. Fends it off towards covers. He is living dangerously.
Fullish delivery on middle, eased to mid on.
Brilliant bowling from Shami, he is on song. Almost a replica of the previous delivery. Mathews is jittery as he is foxed once again. He was lucky to not nick that one.
That's a peach of a delivery! Back of a length delivery around off, hits the deck and seams away after pitching. Mathews fishes at it but is beaten all ends up.
FOUR! Delightful! Fractionally overpitched around off, Perera leans into it and strokes it sweetly through extra cover to find the fence. He is playing the drives really well.
Sharma loses his radar and slips it down the leg side, Dilruwan misses his flick.
Short of a length around off, Mathews pokes at it and gets it off the outer half past cover. A run taken.
Fullish in length around off, played with soft hands to mid off.
Back of a length delivery, defended solidly off the back foot.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Kohli moves to second slip.

DROPPED AND FIVE PENALTY RUNS! That was an easy chance, in fact it is a misjudgement from Dhawan. On a driving length outside off, Perera goes for an expansive drive but ends up getting an outside edge. It is flying towards the slip cordon. Dhawan at second slip tries to grab it with hands to his left but spills it eventually. That was going straight into the hands of Pujara at first slip. To add insult to injury, the ball rolls and makes contact with the helmet that is lying behind the keeper. Perhaps, the two of them were standing very close to each other and that might have resulted in Dhawan's decision to go for the catch. A chance goes down.
Good bowling from Ishant Sharma! Good length delivery around off, a bit of away seam movement on that. Perera gets squared up but manages to block it off the outer half of the bat.

In the air... but safe! That almost carried to the fielder. Fuller length ball in line of the stumps, Perera is early into his stroke and ends up chipping it. Jadeja runs to his right at mid on but he manages to take it only on the bounce.
On a length in the corridor of uncertainty, Perera puts his head down and defends it with a high elbow towards cover-point.
Fractionally overpitched on off, Dilruwan pats it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Perera is playing with freedom! Perhaps the right mindset to play with. Fullish delivery outside off, Perera leans ahead and goes over cover-point to find the fence.

We are back for the final session. 44 overs are still left in the day but the light is already deteriorating. In all probability, only fewer overs will be bowled. Three slips and a gully in place. Mohammed Shami will charge in. Here we go....
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Will this Tea break help Sri Lanka put up some resistance? One thing seems sure. It will help the Indian pace battery to charge themselves up and come out with more vigor and have another go at the visiting batsmen today. Join us at 1433 local time for the resumption.

Earlier, the session saw regular breaks due to the polluted environmental conditions which affected the visitors greatly. Only 10 overs were possible in the Indian innings post the lunch break. That period saw India lose a couple of wickets, which involved that of the Indian skipper as well. After having had enough of these stoppages, Kohli called his batsmen back in the hut to signal declaration.

An action-filled session of Test cricket! India are well and truly bossing the game right now. Sri Lanka had to survive a tricky period of play before this interval but they failed to do so. The Indian seamers came out all guns blazing and were almost literally breathing fire. The first delivery of the Sri Lankan innings saw Dimuth Karunaratne depart, courtesy a brilliant delivery from Shami. He was bowling in right areas and even had Dhananjaya de Silva in trouble before Ishant got rid of him.
FOUR! Edged but runs! Length ball outside off, Mathews gets it off the outer half. The ball goes through the gap between point and gully for a boundary. That's TEA, DAY 2!
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Another delivery outside off, left alone by AM.
Outside off, left alone.
Mathews defends this from the crease.
The experienced campaigner in the side, ANGELO MATHEWS strides out to the middle next. There's no better time for him to get among the runs and show his importance for the side than this one.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Sri Lanka's inability to see off even a small period of play is appalling to say the least. Ishant Sharma delivers a nippy delivery around a good length outside off. It moves in after pitching. Dhananjaya de Silva has been hanging on the back foot ever since he came out to bat today. Does so yet again and pays the price. He looks to defend it from the crease but is beaten on the inside and gets rapped on the back pad. The hosts appeal and umpire Wilson sends the batsman on his way by raising the dreaded finger. De Silva talks to his partner about the review before walking away without opting for it. Sri Lanka are falling a bit too quickly here. The visitors still trail by 522!
Perera defends this from the crease.
Perera looks to defend it off the front foot but gets it off the outer half towards gully.
The batsman goes after a wide one but misses.
Edged but just short! Shami hurls it just outside off, Perera hangs his bat out there. The ball takes the edge and lands just short of first slip. Close shave!
It's been driven superbly through the covers. They manage to come back for the second. No ball has been signaled by the umpire as Shami has overstepped.
Perera taps it in front of mid on and sets off for a run. The fielder there has a shy at the striker's end but misses. The batter would have been in though. A run is completed.

Howzzzat! No, says the umpire. Shami spears it on a length around off, de Silva is beaten for pace as he looks to defend it. Gets hit on the front pad. Shami almost starts running in celebration while appealing only to be halted by the umpire's negation, who indicates that there is an inside edge there. Hold on! There isn't any bat involved as seen from the replays. What's more. Hawk Eye returns three reds too. So if not for the umpire's signal, the Indians would have reviewed that and could have had another scalp as well. Fine things in sport, these.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Perera looks to slash it away to the off side and only makes contact with thin air.
Dilruwan presents a straight bat face as he keeps it out.
Perera punches this off the back foot.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Length delivery outside off, Perera hangs his bat out at that. Gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Another one outside off, left alone.
Outside off, left alone.

Length delivery on the stumps, de Silva looks to pull it from the crease. He isn't in any position to do so and gets rapped on the unmentionable part of the body. He crouches down in pain. He's good to go though.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.

Another appeal, turned down! This one is much fuller from Shami, landing around middle and leg and going further down. De Silva misses the flick and wears it on the front pad. The Indians appeal but after the umpire's decision agree with the same and move on.

A huge appeal from the Indians! Shami hurls this on a length around middle, the ball is angled into the batsman. Dhananjaya looks to flick it but misses and the ball hits his pads and lobs to gully. There were two noises there as the Indians appeal their hearts out. The umpire, however, stays put. The hosts think about the review but decide against it. Replays show that it came off the thigh pad and there was no bat involved. Good that the home side did not review that.
A dot ball to end the over. Perera blocks this from within the crease. 10 runs off the over from Ishant.
Perera stays in the crease and defends that.
FOUR! A bit more authoritative this time from Perera. Fuller outside off, Dilruwan leans into the stroke and drives it through covers. The new ball speeds away to the fence in no time.

FOUR! Not the right lines from Ishant. Strays on the pads with this length ball. Perera stays in the crease and flicks it through backward square leg for a boundary. This is the first one of this innings.
Fuller outside off, Perera drives it through covers for a brace. Sri Lanka and Perera get their first runs on the board.
Sharma starts off with a gentle outswinger outside off, Perera doesn't bother putting bat to that.
ISHANT SHARMA will bowl from the other end. Interestingly, DILRUWAN PERERA will be the one facing him as Samarawickrama isn't fit to bat as yet. Interesting choice of opener from the visitors.
Strays down the leg side, de Silva misses the flick.
Finally sanity shown by the batter. This one is outside off, Dhananjaya shoulders arms to let this one go unharmed to the keeper.
On the pads, flicked towards square leg.
De Silva drives it towards mid on.

Hello! What kind of shot is that first up? Shami bowls a short delivery outside off, Dhananjaya, as if he's batting out there since ages, looks to take him on with a pull. The ball isn't too far from the edge of the blade. Saha thought he had nicked it and puts in a sole appeal. No edge there though.

DHANANJAYA DE SILVA walks in to bat in the second ball of their innings. Remember, this is his first game of the series and what a time to make your way out. This will test his character now. Three slips and a gully to welcome him.

OUT! Dimuth Karunaratne goes out quicker than the time he took to walk out to the middle! What a start for India and Mohammed Shami! The entire Feroz Shah Kotla screams to join the Indian players in celebrations of that wicket. Shami steams in from round the wicket and fires this on a length around off. The ball bounces a tad more as Dimuth gets squared up in his defense. The ball doesn't miss taking the edge of his bat before settling into the safe gloves of Saha. Shami has his arms raised as he runs around to celebrate the success. The slip cordon led by Kohli join him with fist pumps and shouts. India are up and running, the Lankan southpaw departs for a blob.
